correction: No factual correction is established after the follow-up. Both the 5 May ministry draft and the exact government bill estimate EUR 270,000 for adding the entry function to five ePA apps. The government bill additionally requires a costed, jointly financed assessment system under § 360c(2). These sources refute a categorical claim that the entire bill contains no cost estimate or financing mechanism. The author does not expressly make either precise claim: the disputed sentence occurs within its argument that the proposed routing does not deliver a complete, provider-neutral pathway. The matched component estimates and later-system mechanism do not establish that such a pathway is adequately provided for.
effect: The tested allegation cannot presently weaken the author’s request. The cost table alone does not settle the scope of the implementation criticism, predict whether a media break will occur, or establish that the requested architecture is better or worse.
limits: Closing this screening allegation does not endorse the wording or prove a funding shortfall. Its scope remains imprecise. The public record does not establish exactly which costs the author meant, and no intent is inferred. Nor does a larger author forecast disprove the government’s smaller estimate. No actual cost, appropriation, completed system or future service outcome has been measured.
materiality_explanation: Potentially minor if a definite zero-estimate description were established, but that reading is not sufficiently supported. The underlying policy request has separate competition and interoperability arguments. This rejected screening allegation is not counted as a demonstrated error.
direction_explanation: Unknown because no error is established. A literal zero-estimate reading would support the request, but its hypothetical direction is not recorded as an actual favourable error.
context_and_alternatives: The complete October response was already read in round four. This follow-up reread complete physical pages 25–31 and the exact relevant operative provisions and explanations. The author’s immediate subject is the continuity and openness of the digital entry pathway, and its next paragraph criticises a mere reference to the existing booking system.

The official earlier response is authored 18 May 2026, despite a misleading 2025 filename. Its complete relevant physical pages 25–28 repeat the disputed cost wording at page 27. The exact 5 May draft already estimates EUR 270,000 at physical page 114, plus continuing initial-assessment costs on pages 114–115. This does not prove why the language recurred or identify the author’s subjective meaning.

The exact government bill § 345a(1)–(8), physical pages 36–38, goes beyond a bare web link: it imposes integration duties, structured result transfer and a free interface for insurers from November 2027, with the entry service from February 2028. These are requirements, not evidence of completed, adequately resourced implementation.

The exact bill § 360c(2), physical page 51, creates equal KBV/GKV-Spitzenverband funding, detailed annual cost calculations, annual review and arbitration. The memorandum on pages 170–171 includes system provision, staff, updates and training. This is affirmative financing evidence, rather than only a cost-table entry.

The financing mechanism concerns the broader assessment system required from January 2031. It must not be substituted without qualification for the February 2028 pathway using the existing acute-assessment service. The author’s own request seeks broader integration and third-party routes; a complete matched cost model for that requested architecture has not been found.

The author’s dated 4 August press release and four-page August position paper were read in full. They expressly frame the concern as third-party access, interoperability and a complete pathway beyond the KV/KBV structure. Neither defines the disputed cost phrase as a zero in the cost table, and neither supplies a matched quantitative full-pathway funding model.
